Waraq 1.3 — Verification summary
29 October 2026

Tested in Google Chrome through a local preview server on Windows.

Passed
------
- Opened an Arabic EPUB 3 book and an English EPUB 2 book from bundled test data.
- Rendered Arabic text in RTL and the English book in LTR.
- Paged forward and backward; used the chapter table of contents and an internal
  link from one chapter to another.
- Searched Arabic text and displayed results from multiple chapters.
- Added a bookmark and displayed it in the bookmarks pane.
- Restored the last book, reading position, and settings after a page reload.
- Switched to dark mode and changed the font, line height, and text size.
- Entered and exited focus mode with Esc.
- Checked a 390 px wide layout and the sidebar toggle on the narrow layout.
- Showed a clear message when opening a file that is not a valid EPUB.
- Disabled scripts, iframes, forms, and event handlers inside a test book.
  The book frame kept sandbox="allow-same-origin" without script execution.
- Parsed all bundled JavaScript libraries and application code without syntax
  errors.
- Validated reading-data imports: malformed files are rejected, settings are
  bounded, and CFIs and bookmarks survive a JSON round trip.
- Confirmed that the runtime does not depend on libraries or fonts from the
  internet.
- Checked the Arabic interface source for logical Unicode order without hidden
  bidi control characters. Rendering depends on fonts installed on the device.

Limits of this verification
---------------------------
- Direct file:// opening was not automated in the browser tool because that
  protocol was not available; the same content was tested through localhost.
- The native file picker was not automated. Test files were injected through
  the page's demo data instead. Browser permissions were not changed.
- Manual checks are still required for the file picker, JSON import/export,
  drag and drop, and fullscreen in the user's browser. JSON validation logic
  was tested programmatically.
- Not every EPUB file, fixed layout, or browser was tested.
- Sizes reported below are file sizes on disk, not browser memory use.

Version 1.1 checks
------------------
- The core tests above were run for 1.0; the page-layout update was tested in
  Chrome through a local preview on Windows.
- A4 page: approximately 499.90 x 707 px on the test display, ratio about
  0.70707.
- At a 390 px window width: 374 x 528.94 px, with the whole page inside the
  window and the 210:297 ratio preserved.
- Switching between A4 and screen-sized pages worked, and page turning still
  worked after changing the layout.

Version 1.2 checks
------------------
- The app height was tied to the actual visual viewport and recalculated on
  resize; book content could no longer expand the view area.
- Added the fit-page button and the sidebar toggle at all window sizes.
- Checked bounds after layout completed, not during the resize transition.
- At 1366 x 768: the A4 sheet appeared complete at about 402 x 568.54 px.
- At 390 x 500: the sheet appeared complete at about 255 x 360.64 px.
- At a short 1024 x 360 window: the sheet appeared complete at about
  156 x 220.63 px.
- The sheet stayed above the navigation buttons in all three cases. No
  JavaScript errors appeared during rendering or resizing in this update.

Version 1.3 checks
------------------
- Reviewed the public reader at https://epub-reader.online/ and found that it
  uses vertical chapter scrolling with the reading area filled (scrolled-doc).
- Reproduced that mode in Chrome locally with an Arabic demo book. The reading
  area was wide and scrollable, with content longer than the viewport, and the
  rest of the chapter remained reachable.
- Removed the horizontal scrollbar and made the text area keyboard-focusable.
- The final visual preview after that change was not repeated because the
  browser control tool became unavailable. This document does not claim that
  the visual check was completed.
- Logic tests against the application's own functions passed: old settings
  migrate to scrolling, a new A4 preference persists, chapter navigation works
  in scroll mode, and PageDown/End scroll inside the chapter instead of
  jumping to another chapter.
- No book was uploaded to the reference website; its public code was used only
  to understand the layout approach.

Version 1.3 documentation update
--------------------------------
- Rebuilt the project with deterministic ZIP timestamps. Repeated builds now
  produce the same Waraq.html, Sample-Arabic.epub, and release ZIP hashes.
- Added automated checks for the English page title, inline favicon, version
  placeholder, and the absence of remote stylesheets.
- Added a README screenshot captured from the built welcome screen at a
  1000 x 700 viewport in the in-app Chromium browser.
- The demo book's reading view could not be captured in that browser session:
  EPUB.js display timed out with the message "تعذّر عرض صفحات هذا الكتاب".
  The same result occurred with the previously built 1.3 package, so this is
  an environment limitation, not a regression from the documentation update.
  The reading view still needs a manual check in Chrome or Edge.

ملخص عربي
---------
تم الاختبار في Google Chrome عبر خادم معاينة محلي على Windows. نجح فتح كتاب
عربي EPUB 3 وكتاب إنجليزي EPUB 2، وعرض النص في الاتجاهين، وتقليب الصفحات،
والفهرس، والرابط الداخلي، والبحث، والإشارات المرجعية، واستعادة الموضع
والإعدادات، والأوضاع الليلية والتركيز، والتخطيط بعرض 390 بكسل، ورفض الملفات
غير الصالحة، وتعطيل البرامج والموارد الخارجية داخل كتاب الاختبار.

لم تُختبر نافذة اختيار الملف الأصلية آليًا، ولا السحب والإفلات، ولا التصدير
والاستيراد يدويًا، ولا جميع ملفات EPUB أو المتصفحات. جرى التحقق من منطق
بيانات JSON برمجيًا. لا يدعم القارئ PDF أو MOBI أو إزالة حماية DRM.

في تحديث 1.3 أصبح البناء قابلًا لإعادة الإنتاج: تواريخ ZIP ثابتة، وتُنتج
البنية نفسها ملفات متطابقة. تعذّرت إعادة المعاينة البصرية لوضع قراءة الكتاب
في جلسة المتصفح الأخيرة بسبب مهلة عرض EPUB.js، وتكرر ذلك مع الحزمة السابقة،
لذلك يلزم التحقق اليدوي من شاشة القراءة في Chrome أو Edge.
